answers.explain: 'Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.'
'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God.'
Simon, a Galilean fisherman from Bethsaida living at Capernaum, was brought to Jesus by his brother Andrew and renamed Cephas, 'Rock' (Peter).
'That they may all be one': Christ's prayer for the unity of the Church.
Hebrew for 'adversary', the tempter defeated by Christ.
Jesus took bread, blessed it and said 'This is my body': the Eucharist.
A song from the Book of Psalms; one is sung at every Mass after the first reading.
'He is not here, for he has risen.' The heart of the Gospel.
The mountain where God gave Moses the Ten Commandments.
The twelve tribes of Israel, descended from the sons of Jacob.
The table of sacrifice where the Eucharist is offered; it stands for Christ himself at the center of the church.
The consecrated Host is the Body of Christ; 'Lord God of hosts' means God of the heavenly armies.
Bread from heaven that fed Israel in the desert, a sign of the Eucharist.
Judah's exile in Babylon, and our life on earth 'in this valley of tears'.
Our Lady of Guadalupe left roses in Juan Diego's tilma; roses are a Marian symbol.
'A royal priesthood': the priesthood of all the baptized.
'Peace I leave with you': the sign of peace is exchanged before Communion.
A spiritual creature who serves God as messenger; every believer has a guardian angel (CCC 336).
The white baptismal garment: 'you have clothed yourselves with Christ'.
The Sermon on the Mount: the Beatitudes.
'This my son was dead and is alive again': the prodigal son.
The fallen angel who tempted Jesus in the desert.
David, youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, was a shepherd anointed by Samuel, who killed Goliath, served and fled from Saul, and became king first of Judah at Hebron and then of all Israel.
The tower of human pride; Pentecost reverses its confusion of tongues.
Thomas would not believe until he saw the mark of the nails.
'My sheep hear my voice': Christ is the Good Shepherd.
'Your kingdom come': the Kingdom of God is the center of Jesus' preaching.
Israel's land of slavery, and later the Holy Family's refuge.
'I am the light of the world': the Easter candle is lit from the new fire.
'Woman, behold your son': Jesus gives Mary to the beloved disciple.
Placed on the forehead on Ash Wednesday: 'Remember that you are dust.'
Seven sacraments, seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, seven deadly sins.
The star went before the Magi until it stopped over the place where the child was.
The theological virtue by which we believe God and all he has revealed.
A day of celebration in the Church's calendar, ranked below a solemnity.
To call down God's favor; the priest blesses the people at the end of Mass.
Gold, frankincense and myrrh: myrrh foreshadowed his burial.
'I am the vine, you are the branches.'
Elder brother of Moses, appointed by God as his spokesman before Pharaoh.
'Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies…'
The successors of Peter as Bishop of Rome.
The rosary is prayed on beads: five decades of Hail Marys.
Prayer is 'the raising of one's mind and heart to God' (CCC 2559).
The long narrow vestment worn by priests and deacons, a sign of ordained ministry.
Baptism is new birth 'of water and the Spirit'.
The younger twin of Isaac and Rebekah, who bought Esau's birthright and, with his mother's help, received Isaac's blessing.
Solomon built the Temple with cedars of Lebanon.
'For by grace you have been saved through faith.'
To worship God alone; Eucharistic adoration is prayer before the Blessed Sacrament.
'Put on the whole armor of God' to stand against evil.
'The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.'
Lent is a season of prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
The crown of thorns pressed on Jesus' head in the Passion.
The Kingdom of heaven is like yeast leavening the whole loaf.
Ravens fed Elijah by the brook Cherith.
A tenth of one's increase given to God; Abraham gave a tithe to Melchizedek.
'The sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.'
A physical remain of a saint, honored as a sign of the resurrection.
Songs of praise; St Paul urges the Church to sing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs.
'Create in me a clean heart, O God.'
Levite born in Egypt under Pharaoh's death-decree, drawn from the Nile and raised by Pharaoh's daughter.
Christ the King is honored on the last Sunday of the Church year.
The Kingdom of heaven is like a merchant who finds one pearl of great price.
'I am the way, and the truth, and the life.'
A holy one in heaven; the Church canonizes some as models and intercessors.
Jesus called fishermen from their boats to be fishers of men.
From the Latin credo, 'I believe': the Nicene Creed is professed at Sunday Mass.
The sign of our salvation, traced over ourselves at the start of every prayer.
The flood in Noah's day is a figure of Baptism (1 Pet 3:20-21).
'He will come again to judge the living and the dead.'
Jesus told Peter, 'Feed my lambs': the shepherd's charge of the pope.
God's love that forgives; the Sunday after Easter is Divine Mercy Sunday.
The stone rejected by the builders has become the cornerstone.
The widow's two small coins gave more than all the rest.
Easter morning the women found the tomb empty.
Singers who lead the assembly's song; the area of the church where they sing.
The Gloria, the angels' hymn at Christ's birth, is sung on Sundays outside Advent and Lent.
From the Greek for 'the books': the Catholic Bible has 73 of them.
The Spirit descended on Jesus like a dove at his baptism.
Gregorian chant is the Church's own music, given 'pride of place' by Vatican II.
The Magi, traditionally three kings, came to worship the newborn King.
Jesus cast out demons as a sign that the Kingdom had come.
A watch on the eve of a feast; the Easter Vigil is 'the mother of all vigils'.
God's free gift of his own life, poured into the soul through the sacraments.
The son of the promise, born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age and named 'laughter'.
The Sacred Heart of Jesus, symbol of his love, is honored in June.
Sacred images that are 'windows to heaven' in Eastern tradition.
Mid-afternoon prayer, at the hour Jesus died.
Fourth son of Jacob and Leah.
Twin son of Judah and Tamar who 'broke through' ahead of his brother Zerah at birth; father of Hezron and Hamul.
Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham as a wife so that Sarah might have children through her.
Nabal ('fool'), a rich and surly man of Maon with flocks at Carmel, insulted David's men; after Abigail's intercession he was struck by the LORD and died.
Titus was a Greek convert and trusted co-worker of Paul.
Hiram (Huram) king of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's palace and made a treaty with Solomon, supplying cedar, cypress and skilled workers for the Temple in exchange for grain and oil.
Devotion and reverence toward God; one of the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit.

Silas, a leading man and prophet of the Jerusalem church, was sent with Judas Barsabbas to bring the Council's letter to Antioch, and then chosen by Paul as companion on the second missionary journey.
The nave is the main body of a church where the people gather (from navis, 'ship').
Wife of Elimelech of Bethlehem.
The tall pointed hat worn by a bishop.
Presbyter, the Greek word behind 'priest', means 'elder'.
Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours.
An Israelite of the tribe of Naphtali deported to Nineveh, Tobit remained faithful to the Law, gave generous alms and risked his life to bury executed fellow Jews.
Heman son of Joel, grandson of the prophet Samuel, of the Korahite clan of Kohath, was one of David's three chief Temple musicians and 'the king's seer'.
A white linen cloth a priest may wear around the neck under the alb.
Eldest son of Aaron.
Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, was the father of Jeroboam I, who is constantly called 'Jeroboam the son of Nebat'.
Wife and half-sister of Abraham, long barren.
Zadok son of Ahitub, a priest descended from Eleazar son of Aaron, served alongside Abiathar under David and carried the Ark when David fled Absalom.
Uriah the Hittite, one of David's Thirty mighty men, refused to go home to his wife while the Ark and army were in the field.
Jonah son of Amittai, from Gath-hepher, prophesied in the time of Jeroboam II.
Son of Jared in the line of Seth and father of Methuselah.

Tamar, David's beautiful daughter and Absalom's full sister, was raped by her half-brother Amnon and then cast out; she lived desolate in Absalom's house, and his revenge set off the tragedies of David's later reign.
The realm of the dead; Christ descended there to free the just (CCC 633).
Abner son of Ner, Saul's kinsman (his cousin according to 1 Sam 14:50-51), commanded Saul's army and after Saul's death made Ishbosheth king over Israel.
A monastery led by an abbot or abbess, such as the Benedictines of Monte Cassino.
Rebekah's brother in Haran, who welcomed Abraham's servant and later Jacob.
Son of Zippor and king of Moab, who, afraid of Israel camped on the plains of Moab, summoned Balaam to curse them.
Second son of Aaron.
Amnon, David's firstborn, became obsessed with his half-sister Tamar, raped her by a ruse and then hated her.
Asaph son of Berechiah, a Levite of the Gershonite line, was appointed by David as chief of the Temple singers with cymbals.
Amorite king ruling from Heshbon who refused Israel passage through his land and attacked them; Israel defeated him and took his territory east of the Jordan, which Moses gave to Reuben and Gad.
Son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, the spy from Judah who, with Joshua, urged Israel to trust God and take the land.
The Hivite prince of the land at Shechem, from whose sons Jacob bought a field.
Bethlehemite, son of Obed and grandson of Boaz and Ruth, father of eight sons, the youngest of whom, David, was anointed king by Samuel.
A chamber beneath a church, often holding the relics of saints.
Son of Hammedatha (called 'the Bugaean', and in the Greek letter 'the Macedonian'), exalted above all the king's princes.
Son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, called by Deborah to lead ten thousand men against Sisera.
The Church's liturgical rites: Roman, Byzantine, Maronite and more, all Catholic.

Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire, conquered Babylon in 539 BC and issued the decree allowing the Jews to return home and rebuild the Temple, sending back the sacred vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken.
The list of inspired books; also the Eucharistic Prayer (the Roman Canon).
A gathering of bishops to advise the pope or govern a region.
The Passover meal; the Last Supper took place in the setting of Passover.
Levite, son of Izhar and cousin of Moses and Aaron.
A member of a mendicant order such as the Franciscans or Dominicans.
Paul calls the Eucharist the table of the Lord, which we cannot share with the table of demons.
In the Our Father we ask God to forgive our debts as we forgive our debtors.
Jesus announced in Nazareth that he came to proclaim recovery of sight to the blind.
When Peter began to sink, Jesus caught him and asked why he doubted.
Eight souls were saved in the ark, and the early Church saw Sunday as the eighth day of new creation.
David struck down Goliath with a sling and a stone, trusting in God rather than armor.
The Good Thief asked Jesus to remember him and was promised Paradise that day.
Peter warns us to be sober and watchful, because the devil prowls like a roaring lion.
The queen of Sheba came to test Solomon's wisdom with hard questions.
On Holy Thursday the priest uses a basin to wash feet, as Jesus washed his disciples' feet.
Agape is the self-giving love Paul describes as patient and kind.
Fire fell on Sodom and Gomorrah, yet God first rescued Lot.
God spoke to Moses from a flame of fire in a bush that was not consumed.
Paul's ship sailed under the shelter of Crete on its way to Rome.
Look at the birds of the air, Jesus said; your heavenly Father feeds them.
Jesus asks us to abide in him as branches in the vine, for apart from him we can bear no fruit.
Jesus said in his Father's house there are many rooms, and he goes to prepare a place for us.
Visiting the sick and the imprisoned are corporal works of mercy; Jesus says we do it to him.
The first sheaf of the harvest was offered to God, a sign of Christ the first fruits of the resurrection.
Catholics genuflect and kneel because at the name of Jesus every knee should bend.
The Holy Ghost is an older name for the Holy Spirit, who teaches us and reminds us of all Jesus said.
John the Baptist called Jesus the bridegroom and himself the friend who rejoices at his voice.
Tradition places the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor, whose name the psalmist says rejoices in God.
The pope is called the Vicar of Christ, entrusted like Peter with feeding the Lord's sheep.
The first Christians shared all things in common so that no one among them was in need.
Prophets were once called seers, those to whom God showed his plans.
Jesus taught that our yes should mean yes, without needing oaths to back it up.
The spies brought back a cluster of grapes so large it took two men to carry it.
In Egypt the Israelites were forced to make bricks with mortar under harsh slavery.
An early Christian hymn calls, 'Awake, you who sleep, and Christ will shine on you.'
At the Offertory we bring gifts to the altar, first being reconciled with our brother as Jesus taught.
Pride goes before destruction; it heads the list of the seven deadly sins.
Golgotha means 'Place of a Skull,' where Jesus was crucified.
God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths to protect Daniel.
Christ rose on the third day, and the Church confesses one God in three Persons.
The Lord is your keeper, your shade at your right hand.
Marriage is a lifelong covenant; what God has joined together, no one may separate.
Saint Lawrence the deacon was martyred on a gridiron, giving his body to be burned for love.
Giving drink to the thirsty is a work of mercy; even a cup of cold water will be rewarded.
The early Church devoted itself to the breaking of the bread, one of the oldest names for the Mass.
Peter walked on the water toward Jesus until the wind and waves frightened him.
Sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, until Christ conquered it.
A bishop's crozier is a shepherd's staff, a sign that he guards his flock as the Good Shepherd does.
Those who hope in the Lord will mount up with wings like eagles; the eagle is Saint John's symbol.
A soldier pierced Jesus' side with a spear, and blood and water flowed out.
Ezekiel saw dry bones come to life, a promise of the resurrection of the body.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
Jesus looked at Simon, son of John, and gave him the name Cephas, which means Peter.
Saint Sebastian is shown pierced by arrows; the psalm promises we need not fear the arrow that flies by day.
Lent lasts forty days in imitation of Jesus' fast in the desert.
We love because God first loved us.
Logos is the Greek word for 'Word' that opens John's Gospel: the eternal Son who was with God.
Abram left Haran at seventy-five, trusting God's promise.
David danced before the Lord with all his might as the ark came to Jerusalem.
God changed Abram's name to Abraham, father of a multitude of nations.
From the cross Jesus prayed, 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.'
Christmas Mass at night recalls the shepherds keeping watch over their flocks when the angel appeared.
Paul hoped to visit Spain on his way through Rome.
Purim celebrates how God saved the Jews through Queen Esther's courage.
God loves a cheerful giver, which is why almsgiving should come from the heart.
A viper bit Paul's hand on Malta, but he shook it off into the fire unharmed.
Jesus cast a legion of demons into a herd of swine that rushed into the sea.
In Gethsemane Jesus told his friends to watch and pray so as not to enter into temptation.
Priests receive Holy Orders and share in Christ's priesthood, a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
Paul bore the marks of Jesus in his body; Saint Francis later received the stigmata.
John baptized crowds in the Jordan River as they confessed their sins.
In Revelation Christ rides a white horse, called Faithful and True.
In Joppa Peter raised Tabitha from death and later saw the vision of clean and unclean food.
Jesus made a whip of cords and drove the money changers out of the temple.
Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus with a kiss in the garden.
Micah foretold that the ruler of Israel would come from Bethlehem.
Jesus was first led to Annas, father-in-law of the high priest Caiaphas.
Jesus said Tyre and Sidon would have repented had they seen his mighty works.
At the Last Judgment the Son of Man will separate the sheep from the goats.
The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds that grows into a tree.
At Cana Jesus did the first of his signs and revealed his glory.
The altar cloths and corporal are linen, recalling the linen cloths left in the empty tomb.
Jesus said his sheep hear his voice and follow him.
After the shipwreck Paul landed on Malta, where the islanders showed unusual kindness.
The women brought spices to the tomb on Easter morning and found it empty.
Every human being is made in God's image, the root of human dignity in Catholic teaching.
The feast of Weeks fell fifty days after Passover; on that day the Spirit came at Pentecost.
Christians are told not to take revenge but to leave room for God's wrath.
Something like scales fell from Saul's eyes when Ananias laid hands on him.
The Communion psalm invites us to taste and see that the Lord is good.
Jesus told his disciples to be of good cheer, because he has overcome the world.
Jesus calmed a great storm on the sea while the disciples feared for their lives.
Jesus told his little flock not to be afraid, for the Father is pleased to give them the kingdom.
Altar bells ring at the consecration, echoing the golden bells sewn on the high priest's robe.
Jesus said it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter the kingdom.
In the parable of the sower the seed is God's word falling on different kinds of soil.
Jesus said to give your cloak as well; Saint Martin of Tours famously shared his with a beggar.
Herod ordered the massacre of the boys of Bethlehem, the Holy Innocents.
Isaac dug again the wells his father Abraham had dug, a picture of renewing the faith we inherit.
Unless the Lord builds the house, its builders labor in vain.
Confirmation marks us with the seal of the Holy Spirit promised to all who believe.
On Palm Sunday we carry palms, as the crowds did when they welcomed Jesus into Jerusalem shouting Hosanna.
On All Souls' Day we pray for the dead, a practice Judas Maccabeus already called holy.
Joseph interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker in prison.
In Revelation golden bowls full of incense are the prayers of God's holy people.
The prophet Nahum announced the fall of Nineveh.
In the parable an enemy sows weeds among the wheat, which are left until harvest.
Leah named Asher saying 'Happy am I,' and he became one of the twelve tribes.
Pilgrims from Libya heard the apostles in their own language at Pentecost.
The laity share in the royal priesthood of all the baptized, called to proclaim God's mighty deeds.
Scripture asks us to trust in the Lord with all our heart and not lean on our own understanding.
The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus.
Abraham lived in tents as a pilgrim in the promised land, looking for God's lasting city.
Paul was sent to Italy as a prisoner to make his appeal before Caesar.
God promised a land flowing with milk and honey.
Psalm 91, prayed at Night Prayer, promises shelter under God's wings.
Paul reasoned with governor Felix about justice, self-control and the judgment to come.
Herod was king of Judea when the angel announced the birth of John the Baptist.
Like the prodigal son who said 'I have sinned,' true sorrow for sin brings us home to the Father.
Blessed is the one who endures trial and temptation, for he will receive the crown of life.
A leper knelt and begged, 'If you want to, you can make me clean,' and Jesus touched him.
Jesus wept at Lazarus' grave and then called him out alive.
Rabbi means teacher; it is what the first disciples called Jesus when they followed him.
Paul encouraged Christians to aim at living a quiet life and working with their hands.
After the storm God brings sailors to their desired haven, a picture of his peace.
The man born blind said, 'I was blind, and now I see.'
Love, joy and peace head the list of the fruit of the Spirit.
The angel told Joseph to name the child Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.
Monks leave possessions behind to follow Christ completely, answering his call to the rich young man.
God cares so much for us that even the hairs of our head are all numbered.
At Christmas we celebrate the Word becoming flesh and dwelling among us.
We pray to be kept as the apple of God's eye.
Whoever eats Christ's flesh and drinks his Blood in the Eucharist has eternal life.
Terah was the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran.
The census that brought Mary and Joseph to Bethlehem was taken when Quirinius governed Syria.
The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
Proverbs sends the sluggard to learn from the hardworking ant; sloth is a deadly sin.
Kyrie eleison, 'Lord, have mercy,' is the cry of the Canaanite woman we repeat at the start of Mass.
Asked about taxes, Jesus said to render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's.
The psalmist calls all the earth to sing a new song to the Lord.
Some Greeks came to Philip asking, 'Sir, we want to see Jesus.'
The feast of the Chair of Peter (February 22) honors the teaching office Christ gave to Peter.
Christ's seamless tunic, woven in one piece, is read as a sign of the Church's unity.
Hosea's faithful love for an unfaithful wife pictures God's love for his people.
Jesus promised the apostles power when the Holy Spirit came upon them.
Priests blew trumpets of rams' horns as Israel circled Jericho.
Abbot comes from Abba, the word for father that the Spirit teaches us to cry out to God.
Jesus sent the apostles to make disciples of all nations, teaching them all he commanded.
Jesus invites us to learn from him, for he is gentle and humble of heart.
Baptismal fonts hold the water of rebirth, since Jesus taught that we must be born of water and the Spirit.
Cruets bring water and wine to the altar; Jesus first showed his glory by turning water into wine at Cana.
Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought bread and wine, prefiguring the Eucharist.
God led Israel by a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
Paul appealed to his rights as a Roman citizen and was finally taken to Rome.
The Good Shepherd guides us in paths of righteousness for his name's sake.
In the Anointing of the Sick the priest prays over the sick with oil, as James instructed.
Paul compares Gentile believers to wild olive branches grafted into God's tree.
Holy Doors are opened in Jubilee years as a sign of Christ, who called himself the door of the sheep.
Dinah was the daughter of Jacob and Leah.
In the Magnificat Mary praises God who has looked on the lowliness of his handmaid.
Frogs covered Egypt in the second plague when Pharaoh refused to let God's people go.
On the Day of Atonement the high priest made atonement for Israel, a shadow of Christ's sacrifice.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us on the cross.
Jesus promised that whoever knocks in prayer will find the door opened.
Rebekah gave birth to twins, Esau and Jacob.
Pharaoh stopped giving straw yet demanded the same number of bricks.
David chose five smooth stones from the brook before facing Goliath.
Young Samuel answered God's call with 'Speak, for your servant hears,' a model prayer for discernment.
A seraph touched Isaiah's lips with a coal taken by tongs from the altar to cleanse him.
The Pieta shows Mary holding her dead Son, the sorrowful mother who stood by the cross.
On Epiphany many Catholic families chalk the year and the Magi's initials over the door, dedicating the home to the Lord.
Moses lifted up a bronze serpent in the desert, a sign Jesus applied to his own cross.
In the new creation God will wipe away every tear from our eyes.
John saw the new Jerusalem coming down like a bride adorned for her husband, an image of the Church.
God told Joshua to be strong and courageous, for the Lord goes with us wherever we go.
Foxes have holes, Jesus said, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.
The Fourth Commandment tells us to honor our father and mother.
The kingdom is like treasure hidden in a field, worth selling everything to buy.
Saint Catherine of Alexandria is shown with a spiked wheel; Ezekiel's vision of God's glory also has wheels.
We were bought with a price, so Paul says to glorify God in our bodies.
In Revelation the books are opened and the dead are judged by what they have done.
When Jesus died the temple curtain was torn in two, opening the way into God's presence.
A shoot shall come from the stump of Jesse; the Jesse tree traces Jesus' family in Advent.
'Be still, and know that I am God' is a classic call to quiet prayer.
God gives his angels charge over us to guard us in all our ways; the Church celebrates Guardian Angels on October 2.
A taper is a slender candle; at Candlemas we bless candles for Christ, the light for the nations.
The Litany of Loreto calls Mary the Tower of Ivory, borrowing an image of beauty from the Song of Songs.
Jesus promised that the gates of Hades will never prevail against the Church he built on Peter.
John's first letter ends simply: 'Little children, keep yourselves from idols.'
The paten is the small plate that holds the host, the bread Jesus took, blessed and gave as his Body.
Esther became queen and risked her life for her people; Mary is honored as Queen of Heaven.
At the feast of Booths Israel lived in shelters to remember God's care in the wilderness.
Jesus chose to be the guest of Zacchaeus, a tax collector, and salvation came to his house.
Jesus celebrated the Last Supper in a large upper room, where the Spirit later came at Pentecost.
James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, wrote the letter that says faith without works is dead.
Jesus commands us to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us.
The Twenty-third Psalm ends with the hope to dwell in the Lord's house forever.
The walls of Jericho fell after Israel marched around them in faith.
The grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever.
The rising smoke of incense at Mass pictures the prayers of the saints going up before God.
Paul told Timothy not to let anyone despise his youth but to be an example to believers.
Elijah walked forty days to Horeb, the mountain of God, where he heard the still small voice.
Jonah spent three days in the great fish, a sign Jesus applied to his own burial.
Credo means 'I believe'; like the father in the Gospel we profess faith and ask help for our unbelief.
A dogma is a truth the Church solemnly defines, guarding the faith once for all delivered to the saints.
Jesus warned to guard against every kind of covetousness, since life is not measured by possessions.
Saint Bartholomew is shown with a knife; Abraham raised a knife over Isaac until God provided the ram.
Wedding rings are blessed as signs of faithful love; the father gave his returning son a ring.
Jesus was led into the desert to be tempted by the devil, and he conquered with the word of God.
The servant girl Rhoda was so overjoyed to hear Peter's voice that she forgot to open the gate.
At Elim, an oasis of twelve springs and seventy palms, God refreshed Israel in the desert.
Jesus praised the poor widow who gave two small coins, all she had to live on.
Jesus compared his generation to children who played the flute but no one danced.
Revelation's beast from the sea stands for the powers that oppose God and his people.
Lydia, a seller of purple cloth, was the first recorded convert in Europe.
Mary gave birth to Jesus and laid him in a manger because there was no room in the inn.
Isaiah foretold the Christmas child whose name is Wonderful Counselor and Prince of Peace.
Grain offerings were made of fine flour mixed with oil and frankincense.
God fed Israel in the desert with quail in the evening and manna in the morning.
Jesus wrapped a towel around his waist and served his disciples, the model for all Christian service.
John heard the sound of harpists playing their harps before God's throne.
Rahab hid the spies in Jericho and appears in Jesus' family line in Matthew.
The wise virgins kept oil for their lamps while they waited for the bridegroom.
An angel made the chains fall from Peter's hands; his chains are honored at Saint Peter in Chains in Rome.
